chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem if the woman circumambulates without having been circumcised, but as for the man, so he should not circumambulate unless he is circumcised.

key_terms.الْمَخْفُوضَةِ: the circumcised woman (specifically referring to female circumcision)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is female circumcision required for a woman to perform Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of Tawaf by distinguishing between the ritual purity requirements for men and women, specifically regarding khitan (circumcision). While male circumcision is deemed a mandatory prerequisite for the validity of a man's Tawaf, female circumcision is not a condition for women, reflecting the juristic view that the physical state of the male organ is integral to the ritual's validity for men but not for women. This ruling is particularly significant for converts or those who delayed circumcision, ensuring their Hajj remains valid despite the missing act.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem if the woman circumambulates without having been circumcised, but as for the man, so he should not circumambulate unless he is circumcised’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not harmful if a woman who is not Makhfudah (circumcised) performs Tawaf, but a man must not perform Tawaf until he is circumcised.’”
